title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). These endpoints are unauthenticated: staging mints an account-less pending record, and resolve/status exchange the short handle for pairing material without binding or granting anything until an authenticated device authorizes the pairing.

algorithm_list.description: Algorithm ids supported by the target device, sorted by UTF-8 bytewise order and deduplicated before they enter any transcript.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the challenge proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

device_pairing_to_device_challenge_trans.description: Transcript inputs the authorizing device forwards for the to-device pairing path, where no server-staged record exists. The Account Authority rebuilds the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 signing input from these values plus its own gate_audience origin and the digest of the submitted new_device_pubkey; it MUST NOT accept a client-supplied gate_audience, because substituting its own origin is exactly what blocks cross-Account-Authority replay. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2.

transaction_id.description: Verification transaction id of the ak.key.verification.request that carried this pairing challenge.

expires_at.description: Expiry the proof committed to. The Account Authority MUST reject an elapsed expires_at before it verifies the signature.

device_pairing_challenge_proof.description: Proof of possession of the staged new_device_pubkey, bound to the server-minted pairing challenge. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1\n") || canonical_json({client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2. The proof can only be generated after staging returns, because it commits to server-minted values that do not exist at stage time.

transcript.description: Names the exact signing transcript. ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 is the server-mediated short-link path and commits to {client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}. ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 is the to-device verification path and commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. A verifier MUST select the member set from this discriminator and MUST NOT accept a proof whose transcript name does not match the path it is verifying.

kid.description: MUST equal new_device_pubkey.kid. The proof is verified with the staged new_device_pubkey and with no other key. This is a device-local ak:device key id selecting the staged key (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.3), not a DID URL; it is deliberately not named verification_method.

transcript_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical challenge transcript bytes. The verifier recomputes it from its own staged record and rejects a mismatch before checking the signature.

device_pairing_target_attestation.description: Closed possession attestation the target device produces for the accepted_device pairing path, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms: neither the staged record nor the bootstrap carries them, so the approving device reads them here after the signature verifies and copies them byte-for-byte into the ak.device.authorize payload. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1\n") || canonical_json({algorithms, authorization_binding_kind, device_id, device_key_algorithm, device_public_key, hpke_key, pairing_challenge_transcript_digest}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.2. The object is closed over target-owned material plus this pairing challenge, so the target can build it before it knows which sibling will approve and what principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at or scopes that sibling will choose; those values are carried by the approving device Event proof instead. It travels only over the out-of-band channel (QR fragment or to-device message) and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface. It is never a wire field of ak.gate.account.command.pair_device: every member is already recomputable there from the request payload and the Account Authority own challenge transcript.

device_public_key.description: Self-describing did:key form of the same Ed25519 key as new_device_pubkey.key. A verifier MUST reject an attestation whose device_public_key decodes to different key bytes than the staged or forwarded new_device_pubkey.

hpke_key.description: Target device X25519 HPKE public key. This attestation is its authority; a service MUST NOT supply or substitute it.

authorization_binding_kind.description: This transcript exists only for accepted_device pairing. root_anchored genesis and re-anchor keep the full ak.device-authorize-possession-proof-v1 object, and a transcript from one binding kind MUST NOT be accepted for the other.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: MUST equal device_pairing_challenge_proof.transcript_digest of this same pairing challenge. It is the single replay boundary of this attestation: path A commits through it to device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce and new_device_pubkey_digest, and path B to transaction_id, request_canonical_digest, expires_at, gate_audience, pairing_code and new_device_pubkey_digest. A verifier MUST recompute the challenge transcript itself and reject a digest that does not match this pairing.

device_signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the private key of device_public_key over the canonical signing input above. The approving device MUST copy it byte-for-byte into device_authorize_payload.device_signature and into the pair_device request device_signature.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts pending_authorization, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the challenge proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. It also deliberately omits hpke_key and algorithms; those reach the approving device inside the signed device_pairing_target_attestation over the out-of-band channel, so the anonymous staging surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Result of staging a device-pairing short-link record. It returns the full server-minted challenge material the new device needs to build the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 proof. pairing_code is a short human-carryable secret; both device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code are the query credential for the resolve/status endpoints and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query string.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Pairing material handed to an already-authorized device after resolving a device-pairing short link. It carries the server-minted challenge material so the authorized device can recompute the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript and verify the proof it received out of band from the new device. It does NOT carry the proof itself, nor the device_pairing_target_attestation, nor the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs: the staging surface is unauthenticated and never sees any of them, and mirroring signed values here would only create a second, non-authoritative copy. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret; the authorized device still drives ak.gate.account.command.pair_device to complete authorization.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still open, state is pending_authorization. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

authorized_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize Event id. It is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.4.1: before the target device assembles the identity locally it MUST fetch this Event and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key, hpke_key and algorithms, and an expected principal_id, or fail closed.
